model.title: Model

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort level for supported models.
reasoning_effort.title: Reasoning Effort

payload.description: Which market-message profile this agent consumes. 'full' carries every candle tier (daily/4h/15m/5m/1m); 'lean' carries the intraday tiers plus a compact higher-timeframe trend line — the same decisions for a minutes-horizon strategy at ~10% of the prompt tokens.

ChurnConfig.description:
Turnover guard: how much trading cost one agent may burn per hour.

Exists because of a measured incident — a scalper-perp agent booked 140 fills in
two hours for $2.06 of fees (2% of a $100 wallet) against $0.10 of gross P&L. Every
correct-and-profitable per-trade decision still lost money at that rate, so the
guard limits the *rate* in paper as well as live. ``null`` disables one limit;
reducing a position is always allowed regardless (see ``arena.trade_policy``).

max_fills_per_hour.description: Fills per rolling hour, counting every fill including exits (each one pays the taker fee). Trades that add exposure are refused once the hour is full. null disables.
max_fills_per_hour.title: Max Fills Per Hour

cooldown_seconds.description: Quiet period after a fill in a product before the same product may be re-opened. Closing or trimming is never delayed. null disables.
cooldown_seconds.title: Cooldown Seconds

max_fee_burn_pct_per_hour.description: Fee budget per rolling hour as a percentage of equity. Once the hour's fees would exceed it, trades that add exposure are refused. 0.25 = 25 bps of equity per hour; null disables.
max_fee_burn_pct_per_hour.title: Max Fee Burn Pct Per Hour

ExitFloorConfig.description:
No-scratch-exit gate: refuse a close between the stop and the target.

Measured on the real ledger: 29 of 111 exit legs closed at 0-10 bps of profit
against a 10 bps round trip, median move 0.00 bps — two taker fees paid to end up
where the position started. Nothing in a per-order or per-hour gate can see that,
because each fill is legal and cheap on its own; only the distance from the entry
price can. The stop and the target are the two honest ways out of a position, and
a close that is neither is a scratch. ``null`` on either bound disables the band
(nothing to sit between); ``max_hold_seconds: null`` removes the timeout, so the
band keeps applying to a stale position instead of releasing it.

enabled.description: Wire the exit floor into the order path. false leaves exits exactly as they were before the guard.
enabled.title: Enabled

min_profit_bps.description: Profit, in basis points from the entry price, at which a close is allowed. Below it the position has not earned its round trip. null disables the band.
min_profit_bps.title: Min Profit Bps

stop_bps.description: Loss, in basis points from the entry price, at which a close is allowed. Cutting a loss is never refused. null disables the band.
stop_bps.title: Stop Bps

max_hold_seconds.description: Holding time after which the exit floor lets go, so a stale position is never trapped by a move that never happens. null removes the timeout.
max_hold_seconds.title: Max Hold Seconds

ExitFloorConfig.title: ExitFloorConfig

FeeConfig.description:
Trading fee configuration. All simulated fills cross the spread, so only
the taker rate is applied. Expressed in basis points (1 bps = 0.01%).

Default 60 bps matches Coinbase Advanced Trade's base-tier taker rate. Set to
10 for Binance global (VIP 0), 40 for Kraken Pro, or 0 to disable.

taker_bps.description: Taker fee in basis points (60 bps = 0.60%). 0 disables fees.
taker_bps.title: Taker Bps

perp_taker_bps.description: Taker fee in basis points for perpetual-futures products (5 bps = 0.05%, Binance USDⓈ-M VIP 0). Applied to *-PERP fills instead of taker_bps.
perp_taker_bps.title: Perp Taker Bps

LiveConfig.description:
Real-money trading: credentials, which agents may trade, and the guardrails.

Defaults are deliberately the paranoid ones: ``dry_run`` on, a 25% per-order cap,
a 10% daily-loss budget and a 2-orders-per-minute ceiling. ``extra="forbid"`` so a
misspelled limit fails at startup instead of silently not applying.

PaperConfig.description:
How paper fills are priced.

``venue`` snaps every quantity to the cached ``exchangeInfo`` rules (step size,
minimum notional), so a paper run rehearses exactly what the venue will accept and
a rejection in paper is a rejection live. ``simple`` keeps the legacy one-decimal
rule for deployments with no venue data (Coinbase products, offline runs).

instrument_rules.description: venue = enforce cached exchangeInfo rules; simple = legacy 1-decimal rule.
instrument_rules.title: Instrument Rules

PaperConfig.title: PaperConfig

mode.description: paper = simulated fills against the price book; live = real orders on the venue (see trading.live). Defaults to paper: approving live trading is a deliberate config change, never an accident.

binance_perp_symbols.description: Binance USDⓈ-M perpetual contracts to trade, as venue symbols (SOLUSDT). The arena addresses each as <SYMBOL>-PERP so it cannot collide with the spot product of the same name. Empty disables perps entirely.
binance_perp_symbols.title: Binance Perp Symbols
